page.layout: One page of text, with two round portrait medallions above the text (no transcribable text in them except the legends); running head at top centre with page number at top right. Main text in one column, two paragraphs of biography with headings for each poet. No margin notes; footnote-like references are inline.

main_text.l: HOMERVS Græcus Poëta percelebris, clarebat circiter
annum mundi 2838. ante natiuitatem Christi 1124. secun-
dum Cassiodorum. nam Cornelius Nepos in libris Chronico-
rum refert ad longè posteriorem ætatem, puta ad annum mun-
di 3051. ante Christum natum 911. ante Romam conditam
160. annos. Natum itaque Homerum, vt inquit Plutarchus,
belli Troiani tempore, eiusdémque spectatorem fuisse, qui-
dam scribunt, alij 100. annis post, alij 150. Mater ad Meletem
fluuium eum peperit, ob idque Melesigenes appellatus est: po-
stea cæcus factus, Homeri nomen accepit. Duo præcipua poë-
mata scripsit, Iliada & Odysseam. Ilias gesta Græcorum & Bar-
barorum propter Helenæ raptum, sed præcipuè Achillis præ-
clara facinora complectitur. Odyssea verò, Vlyssis ex Troiano
bello in patriam reditum. Scribunt eum obiisse præ ingenti
mœrore, cùm ænigma à piscatoribus propositum non posset
dissoluere: ipsum autem ænigma erat huiusmodi: Quæcunque
cepimus, reliquimus: quæ verò non cepimus, habemus. Vide Plutarc.
in vita Homeri.
HESIODVS Poëta, paulò præcessit Homerum, imò &
coætaneus eius, & sanguine illi iunctus fuisse perhibetur. Certè
Herodotus scribit Hesiodum atque Homerum 400. non am-
plius annis ipsum præcessisse: extitit autem Herodotus circiter
annum mundi 2520. & ante Christum natum 1442. erat He-
siodus ex Ascra, vico Bœotiæ, vnde & Ascræus dictus. Hic pri-
mus ac princeps omniū, de agricultura versibus scripsit, quem
imitatus est Verg. in Georgicis. Scribebat in Bœotia Helladis,
vt inquit Plin. lib 18. cap. 24. de eius morte misera, cúrque à Lo-
crensibus quibusdam adulescentibus sit occisus, vide Plutarc.
in conuiuio septem sapientum.

page.notes: Two round woodcut medallions above the text: left legend "P. POET." and "HOMERVS"; right legend "HESIODVS" and "POETA." Those legends are part of the illustration, not transcribed as text. Some headings above are set in roman body type, not capitals-only headings; they are marked level 3 because they open the poet entries, though they are in running text form. Printed numerals such as "2838" and "1124" are copied as printed. A few words are uncertain due to the scan: "fluuium" and "Melesigenes" look correct; "Bœotiæ" is clear. No words are marked [?] because the print is legible throughout. Note that the printed text uses "s" style long s in the source; it has been written as plain s.
